title: The comparator reaches its completed verdict
statement: For any Boolean input word, any valid input-head position, four finite Boolean words, and any natural number $W$ bounding all four lengths, there are a time $t$ and a Boolean value $b$ such that $0<t\le 2W+2$, and $b$ is true exactly when the sum of the first two words’ values equals the sum of the last two. At every time $j<t$, the machine is not in a completed control; at time $t$, it is in the completed control carrying $b$, with the original words intact and all work-tape heads at zero.
hypotheses_covered: each word has length at most $W$
replaced: For every input word, input position, four words of length at most $W$, there is a time $t$ with $0 < t \le 2W + 2$ and a bit $b$, true exactly when the value of the first word plus the second equals the value of the third plus the fourth, such that no completed control appears before $t$ and at $t$ the comparator sits in the completed control carrying $b$ with all four words unchanged and heads at zero.
